title: Generic agent tab screen
story: "+" on the tab bar used to show "The generic agent tab is not built yet." Now it opens a "New generic agent" dialog: you name the tab, press "Open agent", and Grillo starts a generic agent in the project folder in a tab named "Generic · <name>". From there you paste an email or type your own words into that agent's terminal, as on any agent tab.

checks.criterion: "+" opens the naming dialog, and Open agent starts a generic agent with /grillo-generic in a tab of that name.
checks.steps: Start Grillo and open the made-up project "example-org/sample-project-1" from the Project tab. Press "+" on the tab bar. Type "Sample customer email" in "Tab name". Press "Open agent".
checks.expected: The dialog "New generic agent" with a "Tab name" field, the line "A generic agent can change anything the engine can, after it shows clashes and asks you.", and the buttons Cancel and Open agent; Open agent is greyed out until a name is typed. After Open agent, a tab "Generic · Sample customer email" opens showing a Claude Code terminal that receives /grillo-generic.

checks.criterion: Open agent stays locked while the name is blank.
checks.steps: Press "+", type only spaces in "Tab name", then press Enter.
checks.expected: Open agent stays greyed out, and no agent tab appears.

checks.criterion: With no project open, the dialog asks for one.
checks.steps: On a fresh install where no project has ever been opened, press "+" and type "Sample note".
checks.expected: The warning "Open a project from the Project tab to start a generic agent in it." and Open agent stays greyed out.

checks.steps: With a project open, press "+", then press Cancel.
checks.expected: The project's Map screen, and no new agent tab.
